summary.text: Fulani herders had lived peacefully among the peoples of the upper Benue since the 15th century, but around 1803 a quarrel with the Bata over their customs, in which Ardo Njobbo had a Bata prince killed, turned to war. In 1809 the Ardos met at Gurin, and Modibbo Adama, a scholar who had studied in Bagirmi and Bornu, came back from Usman dan Fodio with a flag as Lamido Fombina, “ruler of the south-lands”. Mounted Fulbe, armed and trained from Hausaland, overcame the scattered, decentralised peoples one by one; Bata of Zummo, Malabu and Holma joined them, while dan Fodio forbade war on the Bata and Verre. Adama took Dulo, capital of Mandara, but could not hold it; Mandara allied with Bornu against him. Fulani sub-emirates rose at Mubi, Michika, Madagali, Moda, Uba and many more, and in 1841 Adama made Yola his capital. At his death in 1847 Fombina stretched deep into today's Cameroon.

moments.title: Ardo Njobbo's quarrel
moments.text: A Bata prince is killed over the Bata's customs; war with the Fulbe follows, and Adama's father dies.

moments.title: The flag at Gurin
moments.text: Adama returns as Lamido Fombina; the jihad begins.

moments.title: Dulo taken
moments.text: Adama takes Mandara's capital, which falls with little resistance, but cannot govern it.

moments.title: The British take Yola
moments.text: Colonel Morland's force takes Yola; Lamido Zubairu escapes to Gurin.
